speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the dizziness you're experiencing? Is it a spinning sensation where the room appears to move, or do you feel lightheaded and faint?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old woman. The patient presents with sudden episodes of dizziness that are position dependent. She describes experiencing a false sensation of motion and occasional spinning, indicative of vertigo. She denies any recent illnesses, injuries, or significant changes in health status, apart from age-related hearing loss (presbycusis).

speaker: Doctor
text: That confirms the vertigo is likely positional; has the spinning sensation lasted only seconds, and do you notice any associated hearing loss, tinnitus, or ear fullness during these episodes? Please also let me know if you have experienced any nausea, vomiting, or difficulty walking.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Episodes of dizziness and spinning sensation. I also have Position dependent vertigo, No recent illness, No hearing loss besides presbycusis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV)

Given the classic presentation of brief, position-dependent vertigo without auditory symptoms, I suspect a displaced otoconial fragment in your inner ear. To confirm this, please perform the Dix-Hallpike maneuver during your next visit, and I will also request an MRI to rule out any posterior fossa lesions given your age.
